body.heading: IIM Ahmedabad PGP Admission 2027–29: Overview
paragraphs: IIM Ahmedabad has released its admission policy for the two-year Post Graduate Programme in Management (PGP) for the 2027–29 batch. For students preparing for CAT 2026, the policy explains the minimum eligibility requirements, category-wise CAT cut-offs, shortlisting criteria and the weightage assigned to different stages of selection.

Meeting the minimum CAT cut-off does not guarantee an interview call. CAT performance is considered alongside academic scores, work experience and other factors specified in the institute's selection criteria.

body.heading: Who Is Eligible for IIM Ahmedabad PGP Admission 2027–29?
paragraphs: Candidates must hold a recognised bachelor's degree of at least three years' duration after Class 12. The minimum graduation requirement is 50% marks or equivalent CGPA for General and EWS candidates, and 45% for SC, ST and PwD candidates.

Final-year bachelor's students and candidates awaiting results can also apply, subject to the institute's documentation and degree-completion requirements. Candidates admitted provisionally must complete their bachelor's degree requirements by June 30, 2027, as specified in the admission policy.

body.heading: What Is the CAT 2026 Cut-Off for IIM Ahmedabad?
paragraphs: The published minimum qualifying percentiles for non-PwD candidates are 95 overall and 85 sectional for General/EWS, 90 overall and 80 sectional for NC-OBC, 85 overall and 75 sectional for SC, and 75 overall and 65 sectional for ST candidates. PwD candidates should check the separate thresholds in the official policy.

These are qualifying thresholds, not guaranteed interview-call percentiles. Applicants must meet the applicable overall and sectional requirements, and shortlisting also depends on the institute's prescribed selection methodology.

body.heading: How Does IIM Ahmedabad Shortlist Candidates?
paragraphs: The raw composite score assigns 65% weightage to CAT 2026 performance and 35% to the normalised Application Rating. The Application Rating considers Class 10, Class 12 and undergraduate marks, full-time work experience and gender-diversity points, as specified in the policy.

The institute then applies its prescribed normalisation process within undergraduate disciplines. As a result, two applicants with similar CAT percentiles may receive different composite scores because their academic records and other application components differ.

body.heading: What Happens After the Interview Shortlist?
paragraphs: Candidates shortlisted for the next stage appear for the Analytical Writing Test (AWT) and Personal Interview (PI). The reported final composite-score distribution assigns 50% weightage to the Personal Interview, 10% to the Analytical Writing Test and 40% to the normalised composite score.
Applicants should prepare to discuss their academic background, career goals and motivation for pursuing management education. Practising structured written responses can also help with the AWT.

body.heading: When Will IIM Ahmedabad Announce Admission Results?
paragraphs: The admission policy tentatively places the AWT-PI shortlist in the second week of January 2027 and final admission offers and initial waitlist information in the second week of April 2027. Candidates should treat these as tentative dates and check the institute's official website for updates.

body.heading: What Should CAT 2026 Aspirants Do Next?
paragraphs: First, prepare across all CAT sections instead of focusing only on the overall percentile. Second, review how your school marks, graduation performance and work experience are assessed under the official Application Rating methodology. Third, start preparing for interviews and written assessments before the shortlist is announced.

Candidates should also compare alternative MBA colleges on eligibility, fees, placement outcomes and career opportunities rather than relying entirely on admission to one highly competitive institute.

body.heading: Final Takeaway
paragraphs: IIM Ahmedabad's PGP admission policy for 2027–29 gives CAT 2026 aspirants a framework for understanding eligibility, qualifying cut-offs, shortlisting and final selection. CAT performance matters, but it is not the only factor in admission.
Official source: https://iima.ac.in/academics/mba/admissions. Verify all numerical criteria and tentative dates against the uploaded admission policy before publication.

items.headline: How composite score are calculated for pgp application at IIM Ahmedabad for PGP (2027-29)?
items.seoTitle: IIM Ahmedabad Composite Score 2027–29: PGP Selection Criteria
items.description: Learn how IIM Ahmedabad calculates the PGP 2027–29 composite score for shortlisting, including academic marks, work experience, gender and CAT 2026 eligibility.
items.author: CollegeDecoded Editorial Team
items.imageAlt: IIM Ahmedabad PGP Composite Score Calculation

body.heading: IIM Ahmedabad PGP 2027–29: How Is the Composite Score Calculated? Who Has a Better Chance?
paragraphs: IIM Ahmedabad Admission 2027–29: Can a student with a 98.5 percentile in CAT get an interview call over someone scoring 99.5 percentile? The answer depends on more than CAT performance alone.

Under IIM Ahmedabad’s official admission policy for the PGP 2027–29 batch, CAT performance contributes 65% to the raw composite score, while the normalized application rating contributes 35%. Academic marks, work experience and gender diversity all influence the application rating.
So, how does the process work—and which of the following three students would have a better chance of receiving an interview call?

body.heading: Three CAT Aspirants: Who Would You Shortlist?
paragraphs: Consider these hypothetical profiles of students targeting IIM Ahmedabad.
bullets: Student A: CAT percentile 99.5; Class 10: 95%; Class 12: 93%; Graduation: 90%; Work experience: None; Gender: Male.
Student B: CAT percentile 98.5; Class 10: 92%; Class 12: 90%; Graduation: 82%; Work experience: 24 months; Gender: Non-male.
Student C: CAT percentile 97; Class 10: 85%; Class 12: 88%; Graduation: 85%; Work experience: 36 months; Gender: Male.

body.heading: Who do you think is more likely to receive an interview call?
bullets: Student A: Highest CAT percentile and strongest academic profile, but no work experience or gender diversity points.
Student B: Slightly lower CAT percentile, with two years of work experience and gender diversity points.
Student C: Lower CAT percentile, with three years of work experience and a relatively consistent academic record.
paragraphs: To answer this, we first need to understand how IIM Ahmedabad evaluates candidates.

body.heading: Stage 1: How Does IIM Ahmedabad Shortlist Candidates for AWT & PI?
paragraphs: In the first stage, IIM Ahmedabad calculates a composite score to shortlist eligible candidates for the Analytical Writing Test (AWT) and Personal Interview (PI).

body.heading: 1. How Are Academic Marks Converted Into Points?
paragraphs: The institute awards rating points for Class 10, Class 12 and graduation based on the following scale. Each academic component is scored separately.
paragraphs_after_bullets: For example, a student scoring 92% in Class 10 receives 10 points, while a student scoring 75% in graduation receives 5 points.

body.heading: 2. How Does Work Experience Affect the Score?
bullets: Less than 12 months of full-time work experience: 0 rating points.
paragraphs: For example, 24 months of work experience earns 2.6 points. Non-male candidates receive three gender diversity points, while male candidates receive zero under this component.

body.heading: 3. How Is the Raw Composite Score Calculated?
paragraphs: The application rating combines academic performance, work experience and gender diversity. IIM Ahmedabad normalizes this rating using the average of the top 50 application-rating scores across the applicant pool.
It then calculates the raw composite score using the formula:
bullets: Raw Composite Score = 0.35 × Normalized Application Rating + 0.65 × (CAT Percentile ÷ 100)
paragraphs_after_bullets: The resulting score is further normalized within the candidate’s undergraduate discipline, using the average of the top 1% of raw composite scores in that discipline.

body.heading: 4. What Are the Minimum CAT Cutoffs?
paragraphs: For non-PwD candidates, the official policy lists these minimum overall and sectional percentiles:
bullets: General / EWS: Overall 95 percentile; sectional 85 percentile.
paragraphs_after_bullets: Meeting these cutoffs does not guarantee an interview call. The composite score and the wider shortlisting process also matter.

body.heading: Stage 2: How Are Final Admission Offers Decided?
paragraphs: Receiving an AWT & PI call is not the same as securing admission. After these assessments, IIM Ahmedabad calculates a separate Final Composite Score (FCS).
bullets: Normalized composite score from Stage 1: 40% weightage.
paragraphs_after_bullets: Final Composite Score = 0.50 × Normalized PI Score + 0.10 × Normalized AWT Score + 0.40 × Normalized Composite Score.
The final selection is based on the Final Composite Score, with candidates assessed separately under the applicable reservation categories.
In short, Stage 1 determines who gets an interview call; Stage 2 determines who gets selected for admission.

body.heading: So, Who Has the Best Chance Among the Three Students?
paragraphs: There is no definitive winner based on these profiles alone.

Student A has the highest CAT percentile and strongest academic record. Students B and C receive work experience points, while Student B also receives gender diversity points. However, the exact normalized application ratings and composite scores depend on benchmarks derived from the applicant pool.
Therefore, ranking these students’ interview chances without those benchmarks would be speculative. Their final admission prospects would also depend on their AWT and PI performance.

body.heading: Key Takeaway
paragraphs: A higher CAT percentile does not tell the whole story at IIM Ahmedabad. Your academic record, work experience and applicable diversity points contribute to shortlisting, while your Personal Interview carries 50% weightage in the final selection formula.

body.heading: Source and Disclaimer
paragraphs: Source: IIM Ahmedabad, Admission Policy for PGP 2027–29 Batch (Domestic), pages 2–4.

Note: The student profiles are illustrative examples, not actual applicants. Exact composite scores and admission chances cannot be determined without the relevant normalization benchmarks and, for final selection, AWT and PI scores.
